bounded_statement: Within the supplied files for case:2c458d2b523ea8c1bd90, the selected result runs an exact two-sided binomial sign test that enters all 20 recording windows as independent trials, even though the data description designates gearbox_id as the independent unit and the 20 windows come from only 6 gearboxes (each gearbox contributing up to 4 rows). The reported rejection of the 50% null (15/20 wins, p = 0.0414) therefore relies on repeated entries of the same independent unit into a row-independent procedure, and the stated conclusion is not supported at the declared unit of independence by the provided workflow.

counterevidence_considered.description: The report transparently discloses that only 6 gearboxes are represented among the 20 windows, so the clustering is not concealed; a reader could in principle discount the claim. This does not, however, change the fact that the test itself treats the 20 rows as independent trials.

The data description also states 'One trial is: one row', which the authors could cite as authorization for row-level trials; but the same description names gearbox_id as the independent unit and stresses clustering, so row-level trials still violate the binomial test's independence requirement.

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I tried to falsify the finding three ways. (1) I checked whether each gearbox in data/input.csv contributes only one row, which would make rows coincide with independent units; instead G-14 and G-33 contribute 4 rows each and G-21, G-47, G-52, G-68 contribute 3 each, so 6 units span 20 rows. (2) I searched workflow/analysis.py for any aggregation, per-gearbox summarization, or cluster-robust adjustment before binomtest; none exists — gearbox_id is only used to count distinct machines for the report header. (3) I recomputed the analysis from the raw data: per-row reductions yield 15 positives of 20 and an exact two-sided binomial p of about 0.0414, matching the report, confirming the p-value indeed comes from the row-level trial count of 20 rather than the 6 independent units. A per-gearbox aggregation (e.g., majority sign per gearbox gives 6 of 6 favoring the adaptive gate, exact two-sided p = 0.03125) is a different procedure not performed by the workflow, so it cannot rescue the stated 20-trial result. All checks confirm rather than refute the issue.

root_cause: The workflow (workflow/analysis.py) computes n_lower and n_windows over raw CSV rows and calls binomtest(n_lower, n_windows, 0.5) without any aggregation, deduplication, or clustering adjustment by gearbox_id. Because windows from the same gearbox share machine-level acoustic characteristics and are declared non-independent by the data description, the effective sample size is at most 6 independent units, not 20, so the binomial trial-count and the resulting p-value of 0.0414 overstate the evidence; the significance claim at alpha = 0.05 is derived from an inflated trial count.
